claims.claim_text: The female appeared extremely frightened and in a state of near-panic.
His demeanor was calm and casual, suggesting he was unconcerned about the police presence.
Officer Milward described the subject as cooperative and forthcoming.
The subject stated he was at the station to visit a friend and appeared genuinely confused about why officers were present.
The subject retrieved what appeared to be a semi-automatic pistol from his waistband, racked the slide in what could be interpreted as a threatening manner.
The action seemed deliberate but the subject's facial expression was difficult to read — it could have been interpreted as angry, determined, or possibly confused.
It was unclear from my vantage point whether the rounds were aimed directly at Officer Milward or fired in a more general direction.
One round appeared to strike Officer Milward somewhere in the torso area.
I immediately drew my service weapon and discharged what I believe was approximately five rounds toward the subject.
The rapidity of events made it difficult to distinguish the exact sequence — it felt nearly simultaneous.
The subject appeared to still be holding a firearm after falling, though visibility was limited due to the fading daylight.
Officers used a K-9 to approach and secure the subject at approximately 1916 hours.
Dispatch informed us that a female motorist had reported being aggressively pursued by a dark-colored sedan from the freeway to the station.
Officer Milward informed the subject he would be with him shortly and walked away.
She stated she felt terrorized during the drive from the freeway and feared for her life.
